title: Disabling Password Expiration for STIG-Hardened Images

blocks.text: This information applies to Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) images that were released on November 24, 2024, and December 12, 2024. STIG images released after these dates are not affected.

If you're using an affected STIG image, passwords automatically expire every 60 days for Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Microsoft Azure, or 95 days (60 days + a 35-day grace period) for VMware.

If the password expires without being changed or disabled, admin access to an App Connector or Private Service Edge is no longer available. When admin access expires, the only recovery method is to deploy a new App Connector or Private Service Edge.
STIG-hardened virtual images affected by password expiration were released on:

blocks.item: AWS and GCP: November 24, 2024
Azure and VMware: December 12, 2024

blocks.text: STIG-hardened virtual images released after those dates are not impacted.
Verify if a STIG-hardened virtual image is impacted:

blocks.item: App Connector
To verify if an App Connector image is STIG-hardened:
Go to Private Access > Private Infrastructure > App Connectors.
Click the App Connector name.
The App Connector drawer opens.

Under Host Platform, if you see ZSIVersion: 2024.11 or ZSIVersion: 2024.12, your image is affected by this issue. If there isn't a ZSIVersion listed or if the ZSIVersion has a date other than 2024.11 or 2024.12, your image is not affected, and you do not need to disable password expiration.
See image.
Private Service Edge
To verify if a Private Service Edge image is STIG-hardened:
Go to Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Private Service Edges.
Expand the row in the table.

Under Private Service Edge Host Platform, if you see ZSIVersion: 2024.11 or ZSIVersion: 2024.12, your image is affected by this issue. If there isn't a ZSIVersion listed or if the ZSIVersion has a date other than 2024.11 or 2024.12, your image is not affected, and you do not need to disable password expiration.
See image.

blocks.text: Zscaler recommends using one of these methods for passwords:

blocks.item: Disable or set a password for AWS, GCP, and Azure.
Disable the password expiration:
Enter the following command (replacing admin with your admin username):
$ sudo chage -M -1 admin
Verify that the password is set to never expire.

$ sudo chage -l admin Last password change : Feb 18, 2025 Password expires : never Password inactive : never Account expires : never Minimum number of days between password change : 1 Maximum number of days between password change : -1 Number of days of warning before password expires : 7
Set a password when creating a new instance using passwd admin (replacing admin with your admin username) and renew it every 60 days.
Disable or set a password for VMware.
Disable the password expiration by entering the following command (replacing admin with your admin username):
$ sudo chage -M -1 admin
Set a password when creating a new instance using passwd admin (replacing admin with your admin username) and renew it every 60 or 95 days.
